challenge.better_approach: Refusing a partial dict was the alternative. It needs every caller to read first, and it still lets a caller drop a field by handing over a stale full dict. Merging at the door fixes the 4bf3 path with no caller change, and all five callers already merge or write the full set.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That no caller needs a key to disappear by omission. Census: ticket.py:126, migrate.py:204, transitions.py:2591 (a fresh cast, nothing standing), ticket_file.py:139 and ticket_log.py:195. None drops a key by omission.
challenge.prior_art: Grepped CairnCommons/tickets for write_state. 0be964512fb0 and 7088856d2150 only use it, and no ticket covers its whole-file semantics. ticket_log.py:195 already merges by hand as {**standing, **state}, so this lifts an existing in-house pattern into the door.
challenge.real_collision: None. Ticket 284798998ab0 split the ticket into plan, state and log, and its docstring says a writer handing over the plan alone leaves the state untouched. This extends the same promise to a writer handing over part of the state.

answers.falsifier: Over a scratch ticket whose state holds workflow_and_state, questions and two berths: a write_state of two keys leaves the other fields byte-equal and the two keys replaced; rewrite_ticket handed the plan plus two berths does the same; a key named in drop= is removed. Wrong intent if a live caller is found that relies on write_state dropping unnamed keys.
answers.from_idea: none, because the trigger is a measured wipe, not a captured idea; the wipe's writer is cairn/tools/base/ticket_file.py (write_state, reached from rewrite_ticket in CairnCommons commit 4bf3b3cb)
answers.how: write_state lays the dict it is handed over the standing state file instead of replacing it. A key goes away only when the caller names it in an explicit drop= argument. write_ticket's split already routes through write_state, so the 4bf3 path (rewrite_ticket handed a plan plus two berths) inherits the fix. Red-first proof in cairn/tools/base/proofs.
answers.traces_to: Law 7: a record of truth is permanent and never silently corrupted. Law 4: the whole-state rule was policy kept by each caller (ticket.py, migrate.py and ticket_log.py each read and merge by hand) and becomes physics at the one door.
answers.what: ticket_file.write_state keeps every standing state field a write does not name, so a partial dict can no longer wipe a ticket's state.

bullets.text: 4bf3b3cb's wipe came through rewrite_ticket: a script read only the plan file and handed back the plan plus two berths, and write_state took the two berths as the whole state.
